reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: Mickey O’Rourke had a go in 2008 and Orlando Bloom earlier this year in “The Cut”, so now it’s the turn of Dwayne Johnson to bulk up and out to deliver a biopic of UFC pioneer Mark Kerr. This is all set at a time when he can make a living for himself and girlfriend Dawn (Emily Blunt) but there are no Ferraris and swimming pools for them. For that he has to win the Grand Prix in Japan and that involves his embarking on the ultimate in fitness and endurance regimes, aided by his own chemical romances that frequently seem to render him little better than catatonic. Domestic dysfunction ensues as he has to face up to his responsibilities and settle his priorities before what he has comes crumbling down. It’s a true story, but it just didn’t engage me at all. Johnson comes across well as the amiable and dedicated athlete, but a film about any sport that requires a rule change to ban eye gouging was probably never really going to work for me. The fight scene are sparing, occasionally graphic, and they do convey just how brutal this mixed martial arts combat can be, but the characterisations here are just all too sterile to engage. Whilst Kerr comes across as a decent human being, Blunt’s performance doesn’t really make anything like enough impact as it trundles along without much from the dialogue to make me care. Tangentially, it does quite enjoyably poke some fun at the inanity and banality of sport’s broadcasting punditry and I didn’t hate it, but I’ll probably never watch it again.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: In the late 1990s, mixed martial artist Mark Kerr strives for world domination in early MMA while battling a crippling opioid addiction and a volatile relationship with his girlfriend.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Set during the late 1990s, former collegiate wrestling champion Mark Kerr rises to prominence in the brutal world of early mixed martial arts. As his dominance in the ring grows, Kerr suffers severe physical pain that leads him into a hidden dependence on prescription opioids. His high-stakes career is further complicated by a tumultuous, emotionally charged relationship with his girlfriend, Dawn. Ultimately, his journey becomes a raw and grounded exploration of ambition, vulnerability, and the harsh personal cost of elite athleticism.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: In 1997, dominant wrestler Mark Kerr enters the world of mixed martial arts during the early, unpolished era of the UFC and Japan's PRIDE Fighting Championships. Earning the nickname 'The Smashing Machine' for his overwhelming physical power, Kerr quickly achieves undefeated success and international notoriety. Behind his fearsome ring persona, however, Kerr struggles with relentless physical agony, mounting career pressures, and profound feelings of insecurity. To cope with his injuries, he grows heavily dependent on narcotic painkillers, initiating a dangerous downward spiral into addiction. His personal life turns chaotic as his volatile relationship with his girlfriend, Dawn, breeds constant turmoil at home. Following a devastating loss, Kerr suffers a life-threatening overdose that forces him into medical rehabilitation. Assisted by close friends and veteran coaches, Kerr works to regain his health and reclaim his place in the fighting world. Though returning to the ring proves grueling, Kerr gradually shifts his focus from maintaining an invincible image to coming to terms with his personal limits. Ultimately, Kerr finds peace in stepping back from the relentless pursuit of perfection, discovering contentment beyond the ring.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Directed by Benny Safdie, 'The Smashing Machine' is a raw biographical drama detailing a pivotal era in the life of former collegiate wrestler and MMA pioneer Mark Kerr. Set between 1997 and 2000, the film highlights the intense, unglamorized early days of the UFC and Japanese PRIDE fighting circuits. Celebrated for his sheer force and grappling prowess, Kerr seems invincible inside the cage, but off the canvas, he faces intense private struggles. Escalating physical trauma pushes him toward severe prescription drug dependence, while his volatile romantic relationship with his girlfriend, Dawn, creates constant friction in his life. Shunning conventional sports movie tropes, the narrative presents a sensitive, compelling look at an athlete confronting his own vulnerabilities, the pressures of fame, and the immense physical toll of his combat sport.
